A prompt is picked at random for each te: A prompt is picked at random for each test request. Leave empty to use the built-in pool. Realistic prompts avoid being flagged as bot probing the way a fixed "hi" is.

Channels that keep succeeding rise in th: Channels that keep succeeding rise in the selection order, and channels that fault sink. Your configured priority and weight stay the baseline and are never overwritten; adjustments live in memory only and reset on restart.
Consecutive faults needed to move a chan: Consecutive faults needed to move a channel down one priority tier.
Consecutive successes needed to move a c: Consecutive successes needed to move a channel up one priority tier. A single fault restarts the streak.
Each validation request consumes quota f: Each validation request consumes quota from the root user and writes one usage log entry, so this budget is shared across all channels in a run.
Headers sent with channel test requests,: Headers sent with channel test requests, so upstreams that only accept a real client (Claude Code, an official SDK) do not reject the test. Grouped by client family: claude / openai / codex / gemini / generic, plus "*" for all. An empty value removes a built-in header. Built-in versions go stale — pick a preset above, then edit.
How far back the success rate looks. Old: How far back the success rate looks. Older requests age out instead of counting forever.
How many already-serving models each run: How many already-serving models each run spot-checks per channel. The cursor advances every run so all models are eventually covered. Set to 0 to disable spot checks.
Ignore the per-channel detection switch: Ignore the per-channel detection switch and check every channel that is not disabled.
Only genuine upstream faults count again: Only genuine upstream faults count against a channel. Rate limits, client errors and configuration problems on our side are excluded, as is synthetic channel-test traffic.
Per-route detail is not available on thi: Per-route detail is not available on this instance yet. It reappears once the channel serves traffic again.
Periodically fetch the upstream model li: Periodically fetch the upstream model list of every enabled channel, confirm each model with a real request, then add new models and remove the ones that stay broken.

Requests a channel needs inside the wind: Requests a channel needs inside the window before its success rate affects weight. Below this the weight is left exactly as configured.
